current criteria (map): The law has been put to work: a decree, regulation or order made under it, or its information commission or commissioner set up, or an existing body it names taking up the oversight.
current criteria (full): Ladder 4 Operating: Yes to 1, 2 and 3: rules made under it, or its oversight body set up. Question 3: Has it been put to work: rules made under it, or the body that oversees it set up? A yes is: A dated decree, regulation or order made under the law; or the information commission or commissioner the law provides for appointed; or an existing body the law names, such as an ombudsman or a human rights commission, reported as having taken up the job.
revised criteria (map): The law has been used: in the past three years a request for information made under it is on record, answered, refused or appealed, or a complaint has reached the oversight body. Rules made under the law, or an oversight body set up, do not reach this stage.
revised criteria (full): Question 3: Has the law been used? A yes is: A dated source from the past three years naming a request for information made under the law, answered, refused or appealed, or a complaint received by the oversight body. A rule made under the law, or a commission or commissioner appointed, is not a yes.

current criteria (map): Public bodies must meet a named international standard: a law, decree, regulation, directive or circular names an international standard on information technology or data and requires ministries, agencies or government systems to meet it. A rule for one sector, a text modelled on a standard, and a system built to one do not count.
current criteria (full): Ladder 4 Operating: Yes to 1, 2 and 3: public bodies must meet a named international standard. Question 3: Must public bodies meet a named international standard? A yes is: A law, decree, regulation, directive or circular that names an international standard on information technology or data and requires ministries, agencies or government systems to meet it.
revised criteria (map): Public bodies apply a named international standard: a source from the past three years names a ministry, agency or government system certified or audited against an ISO, IEC or ITU standard on information technology or data. A rule requiring it, with no body certified or audited, does not count.
revised criteria (full): Question 3: Do public bodies apply a named international standard? A yes is: A dated source from the last three years naming a ministry, agency or government system certified or audited against a named ISO, IEC or ITU standard on information technology, information security, software or data. A law, decree or circular requiring it, or a system said to be built to one, is not a yes.

current criteria (map): The country has taken part in writing international standards on information technology in the past three years: a dated source names the standards body or a public body as a participating member, chair or secretariat of an ISO or IEC committee on information technology or data. An observer seat does not count.
current criteria (full): Ladder 5 Mature: Yes to all four: the country has taken part in writing such standards in the last three years. Question 4: Has the country taken part in writing international standards on information technology in the last three years? A yes is: A dated source naming the standards body or a public body as a participating member, chair or secretariat of an ISO or IEC committee that writes standards on information technology or data. An observer seat is not a yes.
revised criteria (map): Public bodies are held to international standards: a rule requires them to meet a named international standard on information technology or data, and a source from the past three years names three or more public bodies or systems certified or audited against such a standard, or counts them.
revised criteria (full): Question 4: Are public bodies held to it across government? A yes is: A law, decree, regulation, directive or circular requiring ministries, agencies or government systems to meet a named international standard on information technology or data, and a dated source from the last three years naming three or more public bodies or systems certified or audited against such a standard, or counting them. A seat on an ISO or IEC committee is not a yes.

current criteria (map): A law on AI itself is in force and applies across sectors.
current criteria (full): Ladder 4 Operating: Yes to 1, 2 and 3: a law on AI itself in force. Question 3: Is there a law in force on AI itself, and not only for one sector or one use? A yes is: An AI act, decree or regulation in force that applies to AI across sectors.
revised criteria (map): A law on AI itself, applying across sectors, is in force and has been applied in the past three years: the body it names has registered, licensed, decided on or penalised an AI system or provider, or a court has applied it. A regulation made under it does not count.
revised criteria (full): Question 3: Is a law on AI itself in force, and has it been applied? A yes is: An AI act, decree or regulation in force that applies across sectors, and in the last three years a dated registration, licence, decision or penalty by the body it names, or a court ruling applying it. A regulation or order made under the law is not a yes.

current criteria (map): That law has been applied in the past three years: a regulation or order has been made under it, or the body it names has registered, licensed, decided or penalised.
current criteria (full): Ladder 5 Mature: Yes to all four: that law has been applied in the last three years. Question 4: Has that law been applied in the last three years? A yes is: A dated regulation or order made under it, or a dated registration, licence, decision or penalty by the body it names.
revised criteria (map): The law is in regular use: the body it names publishes a register or count of the AI systems or providers it has registered, licensed, decided on or penalised, for a period ending within the past two years.
revised criteria (full): Question 4: Is the law in regular use? A yes is: A register or count, published by the body the law names, of the registrations, licences, decisions or penalties made under it, for a period ending within the last two years. Two or three cases named one by one are not a yes.

current criteria (map): The government has named a body to carry out the strategy: a council, office, agency, committee or ministry unit set up or named for it.
current criteria (full): Ladder 4 Operating: Yes to 1, 2 and 3: a body is named to carry it out. Question 3: Has the government named a body to carry it out? A yes is: A council, office, agency, committee or ministry unit set up or named to carry out the strategy, by an instrument or reported at work.
revised criteria (map): The strategy is being carried out: in the past three years an action it names has started, such as a programme, institution, law or project that a source ties to the strategy. A body named to carry it out, or money allocated with nothing started, does not reach this stage.
revised criteria (full): Question 3: Has an action in the strategy started? A yes is: In the last three years: a dated source naming a programme, institution, law or project that it ties to the strategy as started, launched or in service. A body named to carry out the strategy, or money allocated with nothing started, is not a yes.

current criteria (map): Public money has gone into carrying out the strategy in the past three years: a dated source names money allocated to it, or an action in it started with its funding named. How good the strategy is, is not judged.
current criteria (full): Ladder 5 Mature: Yes to all four: public money has gone into carrying it out. Question 4: Has the government put money into carrying it out? A yes is: In the last three years: a dated source naming public money allocated to the strategy, or an action in the strategy started with funding named.
revised criteria (map): Results are published against the strategy: in the past three years the government or the body carrying it out has reported progress against the strategy's own actions or targets, or published a review of it. How good the strategy is, is not judged.
revised criteria (full): Question 4: Has progress against the strategy been reported? A yes is: In the last three years: a published progress report, review or evaluation giving what has been done against the strategy's own actions or targets.

current criteria (map): E-procurement runs from tender to award or payment, or is required of all public bodies.
current criteria (full): Ladder 4 End to end: Yes to 3. Question 3: Does it run end to end across government? A yes is: A source from the last three years says e-procurement runs from tender to award or payment, or is required of all public bodies.
revised criteria (map): E-procurement is used from tender to award or payment by ministries or agencies across government, named by a source from the past three years. A requirement that all public bodies use it does not reach this stage.
revised criteria (full): Question 3: Is it used end to end across government? A yes is: A source from the last three years says ministries or agencies across government buy through the system from tender to award or payment, or names several doing so. A rule requiring all public bodies to use it is not a yes.

current criteria (map): Money has been committed to the plan in the past three years: a budget line, a universal service fund allocation or a financed programme that the source ties to the plan.
current criteria (full): Ladder 4 Operating: Yes to 1, 2 and 3: money is committed to the plan. Question 3: Is money committed to it? A yes is: In the last three years: a budget line, a universal service fund allocation or a financed programme that the source ties to the plan.
revised criteria (map): The plan is being carried out: in the past three years a programme, universal service fund project or financed project that the source ties to the plan has connected sites, built towers or fibre, or brought people online. Money committed with nothing built or connected does not reach this stage.
revised criteria (full): Question 3: Is the plan being carried out? A yes is: In the last three years: a dated source naming sites connected, towers or fibre built, or people brought online by a programme, universal service fund project or financed project that it ties to the plan. A budget line or allocation with nothing built or connected is not a yes.

current criteria (map): The plan is funded, and the government has published figures against the plan's own targets in the past three years. Whether the targets are met is not judged.
current criteria (full): Ladder 5 Mature: Yes to all four: the plan is funded and progress against its targets is published. Question 4: Does the government publish progress against the plan's targets? A yes is: In the last three years: a published review or report giving figures against the plan's own targets.
revised criteria (map): The plan is being carried out, and the government has published figures against the plan's own targets in the past three years. Whether the targets are met is not judged.
revised criteria (full): Ladder 5: yes to all four, the plan being carried out (revised question 3) and progress against its targets published. Question 4 unchanged.

current criteria (map): The register holds the beneficial owners of every company in the country, and a firm's number is shared with tax or social security.
current criteria (full): Ladder 5 Beneficial owners: Yes to 4. Question 4: Are the beneficial owners of every company recorded? A yes is: A source from the last three years says the register holds the beneficial owners of all companies in the country: filing is complete, not only required or under way.
revised criteria (map): The register holds the beneficial owners of every company, and they are consulted: a source from the past three years reports banks, the tax authority or other public bodies using the register's beneficial-ownership records, or counts searches of them.
revised criteria (full): Question 4: Are the beneficial owners recorded and consulted? A yes is: A source from the last three years says the register holds the beneficial owners of all companies in the country, filing complete, and reports banks, the tax authority or other public bodies consulting those records, or counts searches of them.

current criteria (map): A financial ombudsman or a regulator's complaints unit takes complaints about digital financial services.
current criteria (full): Ladder 4 Complaints handled: Yes to 3. Question 3: Does a body take complaints? A yes is: A source from the last three years says a financial ombudsman or a regulator's complaints unit takes complaints about digital financial services.
revised criteria (map): Complaints about digital financial services have been handled: in the past three years a financial ombudsman or a regulator's complaints unit has received, investigated or settled one. A unit that may take complaints, with none on record, does not reach this stage.
revised criteria (full): Question 3: Has a body handled complaints? A yes is: A source from the last three years says a financial ombudsman or a regulator's complaints unit has received, investigated or settled complaints about digital financial services.

current criteria (map): A body is designated by law or decree with a mandate over AI harms or AI systems.
current criteria (full): Ladder 4 Authority: Yes to 3. Question 3: Is an authority designated? A yes is: A source from the last three years says a body is designated by law or decree with a mandate over AI harms or AI systems.
revised criteria (map): A rule on AI harms has been used: in the past three years a regulator or other body has received a complaint, opened an investigation or issued a warning about a harm from AI under it. A body designated with nothing done does not reach this stage.
revised criteria (full): Question 3: Has the rule been used? A yes is: A source from the last three years naming a complaint received, an investigation opened or a warning issued about a harm from AI, under a rule in force or by a body with a mandate over AI. A body designated by law or decree, with no such act on record, is not a yes.

current criteria (map): As stage 3, and the authority has published a way to send data without asking: a list of countries data may go to, model contract terms, or a general authorisation.
current criteria (full): Ladder 4 Operating: Workable: yes to 1, 2 and 3. Question 3: Is there a published way to send data without asking? A yes is: A dated source saying the authority has published a list of countries data may go to, model contract terms, or a general authorisation covering a class of transfers. A form or procedure for applying for permission is not a yes.
revised criteria (map): As stage 3, and data goes abroad by a published route: in the past three years the authority has authorised transfers or received transfer notifications, or a source names an organisation sending data under its list of countries, model terms or general authorisation.
revised criteria (full): Question 3: Is data sent abroad by a published route? A yes is: In the last three years: a dated source saying the authority authorised transfers or received transfer notifications, or naming an organisation sending personal data abroad under the authority's list of countries, model contract terms or general authorisation. A list or terms published, with no transfer on record, is not a yes.

current criteria (map): As stage 4, and the country is open to its African partners: it has ratified the AfCFTA Digital Trade Protocol or the Malabo Convention, or treats a regional partner's protection as good enough in practice.
current criteria (full): Ladder 5 Mature: Open to Africa: yes to all four. Question 4: Is the country open to its African partners? A yes is: The country has ratified the AfCFTA Digital Trade Protocol or the Malabo Convention, or a source says it treats a regional partner's protection as good enough and that is applied.
revised criteria (map): As stage 4, and data goes to African partners in practice: personal data is reported sent to another African country under the rule in the past three years, the country having ratified the AfCFTA Digital Trade Protocol or the Malabo Convention, or treating that partner's protection as good enough.
revised criteria (full): Question 4: Does data go to African partners under the rule? A yes is: In the last three years: a dated source naming personal data sent to another African country under the rule, and the country has ratified the AfCFTA Digital Trade Protocol or the Malabo Convention, or treats that partner's protection as good enough. Ratification alone is not a yes.

current criteria (map): The country takes part in PAPSS or a regional payment system in service.
current criteria (full): Ladder 4 Regional system: Yes to 3. Question 3: Is the country in a regional payment system? A yes is: A source from the last three years says the country takes part in PAPSS or a regional payment system in service.
revised criteria (map): Payments to or from the country pass through PAPSS or a regional payment system: its banks or payment providers send and receive through it. Joining one does not reach this stage.
revised criteria (full): Question 3: Do the country's payments go through a regional payment system? A yes is: A source from the last three years says the country's banks or payment providers send and receive payments through PAPSS or a regional payment system in service. Membership or joining alone is not a yes.

current criteria (map): A body is named to carry out the policy: a council, office, agency, committee, chief data officer or ministry unit set up or named for it. The ministry that wrote the policy being responsible for it in general does not count.
current criteria (full): Ladder 4 Operating: Yes to 1, 2 and 3: a body is named to carry it out. Question 3: Has the government named a body to carry it out? A yes is: A council, office, agency, committee, chief data officer or ministry unit set up or named to carry out the policy, by an instrument or reported at work.
revised criteria (map): The policy is being applied: in the past three years a public body named by a source has classified, catalogued or shared data under it. A body named to carry it out, with nothing done, does not reach this stage.
revised criteria (full): Question 3: Is the policy being applied? A yes is: In the last three years: a dated source naming a public body that has classified, catalogued or shared data under the policy or a rule made under it. A council, office or chief data officer set up, with no such act on record, is not a yes.

current criteria (map): A rule or standard the policy called for has been issued in the past three years: a law, regulation, standard or guideline, such as one on classifying data or on sharing it between public bodies. How good the policy is, and whether it follows the African Union's framework, is not judged.
current criteria (full): Ladder 5 Mature: Yes to all four: a rule or standard the policy called for has been issued. Question 4: Has the government issued a rule or standard the policy called for? A yes is: In the last three years: a dated source naming a law, regulation, standard or guideline issued under the policy, such as one on classifying data, on sharing data between public bodies or on publishing data.
revised criteria (map): Public bodies across government manage or share data under the policy: a source from the past three years names three or more ministries or agencies doing so, or counts them. How good the policy is, and whether it follows the African Union's framework, is not judged.
revised criteria (full): Question 4: Is it applied across government? A yes is: In the last three years: a dated source naming three or more ministries or agencies classifying, cataloguing or sharing data under the policy or its rules, or counting them. A rule or standard issued, with no one named using it, is not a yes.

current criteria (map): Public bodies are required to follow the framework: a decree, law, regulation or circular makes it compulsory and names the body that enforces it.
current criteria (full): Ladder 4 Operating: Yes to 1, 2 and 3: public bodies are required to follow it. Question 3: Are public bodies required to follow it? A yes is: A decree, law, regulation or circular that makes the framework compulsory for public bodies and names the body that enforces it.
revised criteria (map): Public bodies use the framework: a dated source from the past three years names a ministry, agency or system exchanging data under it or certified as meeting it.
revised criteria (full): Question 3: Is a public body using it? A yes is: In the last three years: a dated source naming a ministry, agency or system that exchanges data under the framework, or that has been certified as meeting it. A decree making it compulsory, with no one named using it, is not a yes.

current criteria (map): Public bodies are following the framework in the past three years: a dated source names or counts the ministries, agencies or systems that exchange data under it or are certified as meeting it. How good the framework is, is not judged.
current criteria (full): Ladder 5 Mature: Yes to all four: public bodies are following it. Question 4: Are public bodies following it? A yes is: In the last three years: a dated source naming or counting ministries, agencies or systems that exchange data under the framework, or that have been certified as meeting it.
revised criteria (map): Use is required and wide: a decree, law, regulation or circular makes the framework compulsory and names who enforces it, and a source from the past three years names three or more ministries, agencies or systems exchanging data under it, or counts them. How good the framework is, is not judged.
revised criteria (full): Question 4: Is its use required and wide? A yes is: A decree, law, regulation or circular making the framework compulsory for public bodies and naming its enforcer, and in the last three years a dated source naming three or more ministries, agencies or systems exchanging data under it or certified as meeting it, or counting them.

current criteria (map): A body is named to enforce the rule: a regulator, agency or ministry unit that checks compliance or grants exemptions. A regulator that issued the rule for the bodies it licenses counts.
current criteria (full): Ladder 4 Operating: Yes to 1, 2 and 3: a body is named to enforce it. Question 3: Has a body been named to enforce it? A yes is: A regulator, agency or ministry unit that the rule or a source says checks compliance or grants exemptions. A regulator that issued the rule for the bodies it licenses counts.
revised criteria (map): The rule has been used: in the past three years the body enforcing it has checked compliance or received notifications under it, or a source names an organisation keeping data in the country because of it. A body named with nothing done does not reach this stage.
revised criteria (full): Question 3: Has the rule been used? A yes is: In the last three years: a dated source naming a compliance check or notification under the rule by the body that enforces it, or an organisation that keeps data in the country because the rule requires it.

current criteria (map): The government has named where public bodies must host: a government cloud or data centre in service that the policy tells them to use, or a published list of approved providers.
current criteria (full): Ladder 4 Operating: Yes to 1, 2 and 3: the government has named where public bodies must host. Question 3: Has the government named where public bodies must host? A yes is: A government cloud or data centre in service that the policy tells public bodies to use, or a published list of approved or accredited providers.
revised criteria (map): Public bodies use the named hosting: a government cloud or data centre the policy tells them to use, or an approved provider, hosts at least one ministry's or agency's systems, by a source from the past three years. A hosting named with no one on it does not reach this stage.
revised criteria (full): Question 3: Has a public body moved onto the named hosting? A yes is: In the last three years: a dated source naming a ministry or agency whose systems are hosted in the government cloud or data centre the policy names, or with a provider on its approved list.

current criteria (map): Public bodies have moved onto the named hosting in the past three years: a dated source names or counts the ministries or agencies that have. How good the policy is, is not judged.
current criteria (full): Ladder 5 Mature: Yes to all four: public bodies have moved onto the named hosting. Question 4: Have public bodies moved onto it? A yes is: In the last three years: a dated source naming or counting ministries or agencies whose systems have moved to the named hosting under the policy.
revised criteria (map): Public bodies across government have moved onto the named hosting in the past three years: a dated source names three or more ministries or agencies that have, or counts them. How good the policy is, is not judged.
revised criteria (full): Question 4: Have public bodies across government moved onto it? A yes is: In the last three years: a dated source naming three or more ministries or agencies whose systems have moved to the named hosting under the policy, or counting them.

current criteria (map): The programme is open to or required of civil servants in all ministries, or has trained staff across most of government.
current criteria (full): Ladder 4 Across government: Yes to 3. Question 3: Does it reach across government? A yes is: A source from the last three years says the programme is open to or required of civil servants in all ministries, or has trained staff across most of government.
revised criteria (map): Civil servants across most of government have been trained through the programme, by a source from the past three years. A programme open to, or required of, every ministry does not reach this stage on that alone.
revised criteria (full): Question 3: Has it reached across government? A yes is: A source from the last three years says the programme has trained staff in most ministries, or across most of government. A programme open to or required of civil servants in all ministries, with no training across government on record, is not a yes.

current criteria (map): Companies that are not banks can be licensed under the law or rules in force to offer payments or issue e-money: a source says so, or names one licensed.
current criteria (full): Ladder 4 Operating: Yes to 1, 2 and 3: companies that are not banks can be licensed under it. Question 3: Can a company that is not a bank be licensed under it to offer payments? A yes is: A source says the law or rules in force license payment providers or e-money issuers that are not banks, or names one licensed under them.
revised criteria (map): A company that is not a bank is licensed under the law or rules in force and offers payments or e-money: a source names one. Rules that would allow it, with none licensed, do not reach this stage.
revised criteria (full): Question 3: Is a company that is not a bank licensed under it and operating? A yes is: A source naming a payment provider or e-money issuer that is not a bank, licensed under the law or rules in force and offering its service.

current criteria (map): A rule requires mobile money providers and banks to connect to each other or to a national or regional switch. A switch that providers may join by choice, or a rule that binds banks only, does not reach this stage.
current criteria (full): Ladder 5 Mature: Yes to all four: a rule requires providers to connect to each other. Question 4: Does a rule require payment providers to connect to each other? A yes is: A dated rule in force that mobile money providers and banks must connect to each other or to a national or regional switch.
revised criteria (map): Providers are connected because a rule requires it: a rule in force requires mobile money providers and banks to connect to each other or to a national or regional switch, and a source from the past three years shows payments flowing between them under it. A switch providers may join by choice, or a rule that binds banks only, does not reach this stage.
revised criteria (full): Question 4: Are providers connected under a rule requiring it? A yes is: A dated rule in force that mobile money providers and banks must connect to each other or to a national or regional switch, and a source from the last three years showing payments flowing between them, or naming providers connected under it.

current criteria (map): A government contract or agreement with a foreign provider or partner includes terms on data jurisdiction, portability, exit or handing over source code.
current criteria (full): Ladder 5 Contract terms: Yes to 4. Question 4: Do contracts carry data terms? A yes is: A source from the last three years says a government contract or agreement with a foreign provider or partner includes terms on data jurisdiction, portability, exit or handing over source code.
revised criteria (map): Data terms in contracts have been used: in the past three years the government has moved data or a system from a foreign provider, taken back source code, or invoked exit or jurisdiction terms in a contract.
revised criteria (full): Question 4: Have contract data terms been used? A yes is: A source from the last three years says the government moved data or a system away from a foreign provider, received source code handed over, or invoked terms on data jurisdiction, portability or exit in a contract. Terms written into a contract, with nothing done under them, are not a yes.

current criteria (map): 50 per cent or more of secondary schools have internet for teaching, and digital literacy or computing is a compulsory subject in the national secondary curriculum.
current criteria (full): Ladder 5 Mature: Yes to 3 and 4. Question 4: Is digital literacy or computing compulsory in the secondary curriculum? A yes is: A source from the last three years says digital literacy, ICT or computing is a compulsory subject in the national secondary curriculum.
revised criteria (map): 50 per cent or more of secondary schools have internet for teaching, and digital literacy or computing is taught as a compulsory subject, with a count or share of the schools or learners taking it from the past three years.
revised criteria (full): Question 4: Is digital literacy or computing compulsory and taught? A yes is: A source from the last three years saying digital literacy, ICT or computing is a compulsory subject in the national secondary curriculum, and giving a count or share of the schools teaching it or the learners taking it.

current criteria (map): A decree, regulation or order has been made under the law: on electronic signatures, on those who certify them, or on those who sell online.
current criteria (full): Ladder 4 Operating: Yes to 1, 2 and 3: rules made under it. Question 3: Have rules been made under it to put it to work? A yes is: A dated decree, regulation or order made under the law: on electronic signatures, on those who certify them, or on those who sell online.
revised criteria (map): The law is in use: in the past three years a provider of electronic signatures or certificates is accredited or licensed under it, or an online seller registered or licensed under it. A decree made under the law alone does not reach this stage.
revised criteria (full): Question 3: Has the law been used? A yes is: A dated accreditation or licence of a provider of electronic signatures or certificates under the law, or a registration or licence of an online seller or digital operator under it, in the last three years. A decree, regulation or order made under the law is not a yes.

current criteria (map): The law has been applied in the past three years: a provider of electronic signatures accredited or licensed under it, online sellers registered or licensed, or an order or penalty made. A government office using electronic signatures does not reach this stage.
current criteria (full): Ladder 5 Mature: Yes to all four: the law applied in the last three years. Question 4: Has it been applied in the last three years? A yes is: A dated accreditation or licence of a provider of electronic signatures or certificates under it, a registration or licence of an online seller or digital operator under it, or a penalty or order made under it.
revised criteria (map): The law is in regular use: in the past three years a count of certificates issued or online sellers registered under it is published, or an order, penalty or court ruling is made under it. A government office using electronic signatures does not reach this stage.
revised criteria (full): Question 4: Is the law in regular use? A yes is: In the last three years: a published count of electronic certificates issued, signature providers accredited or online sellers registered under the law, or a dated order, penalty or court ruling made under it.

current criteria (map): The roll was published or open to voters to check, online, by text message or at centres.
current criteria (full): Ladder 4 Open for checking: Yes to 3. Question 3: Can voters check the roll? A yes is: A source from the last three years says the roll was published or open to voters to check, online, by text message or at centres.
revised criteria (map): The digital roll has been used: at the latest national election voters were identified against it at polling stations, or voters checked their entries online, by text message or at centres, with a source saying they did.
revised criteria (full): Question 3: Has the digital roll been used? A yes is: A source from the last three years says voters were identified against the digital or biometric roll at polling stations, or that voters checked their entries online, by text message or at centres. A roll published or open to checking, with no use reported, is not a yes.

current criteria (map): Refugees or internally displaced people may register SIM cards, open mobile money or bank accounts, or enrol in the national digital ID, by law or in practice.
current criteria (full): Ladder 4 Digital access: Yes to 3. Question 3: Can they use digital services? A yes is: A source from the last three years says refugees or internally displaced people may register SIM cards, open mobile money or bank accounts, or enrol in the national digital ID, by law or in practice.
revised criteria (map): Refugees or displaced people are using digital services: a source from the past three years reports them registering SIM cards, opening mobile money or bank accounts, or enrolling in the national digital ID. Being allowed to does not reach this stage.
revised criteria (full): Question 3: Are they using digital services? A yes is: A source from the last three years reporting refugees or internally displaced people registering SIM cards, opening mobile money or bank accounts, or enrolling in the national digital ID. A law or policy allowing it, with no use reported, is not a yes.

current criteria (map): Lawyers or litigants can file cases or documents with the courts online.
current criteria (full): Ladder 4 Online filing: Yes to 3. Question 3: Can cases be filed online? A yes is: A source from the last three years says lawyers or litigants can file cases or documents with the courts online.
revised criteria (map): Cases or documents are filed with the courts online: a source from the past three years reports e-filing in use in named courts, or counts cases filed online. E-filing that is possible but unused does not reach this stage.
revised criteria (full): Question 3: Are cases filed online? A yes is: A source from the last three years reporting lawyers or litigants filing cases or documents online in named courts, or counting cases filed online. A portal that allows filing, with no filing reported, is not a yes.

current criteria (map): Court decisions are published online or the public can look up a case's status online.
current criteria (full): Ladder 5 Open online: Yes to 4. Question 4: Are judgments or case status open online? A yes is: A source from the last three years says court decisions are published online or the public can look up a case's status online.
revised criteria (map): The courts' systems are used at scale: a source from the past three years counts cases filed or managed electronically, and court decisions or case status are open to the public online.
revised criteria (full): Question 4: Are the courts' systems used at scale and open? A yes is: A source from the last three years giving a count of cases filed or managed electronically, and court decisions published online or case status open to public look-up online.

current criteria (map): Land searches, title applications or transfers can be made online.
current criteria (full): Ladder 5 Online: Yes to 4. Question 4: Can people search or register land online? A yes is: A source from the last three years says land searches, title applications or transfers can be made online.
revised criteria (map): Land searches, title applications or transfers are made online: a source from the past three years counts them or reports them in routine use.
revised criteria (full): Question 4: Do people search or register land online? A yes is: A source from the last three years counting land searches, title applications or transfers made online, or reporting them in routine use. A service that allows it, with no use reported, is not a yes.

current criteria (map): The law in force provides for a digital identity: a biometric register, an identity number unique to each person, or an identity that can be checked electronically. A law for a paper card only does not reach this stage.
current criteria (full): Ladder 4 Operating: Yes to 1, 2 and 3: the law in force provides for a digital identity. Question 3: Does the law provide for a digital identity? A yes is: A source says the law in force sets up a biometric register, an identity number unique to each person, or an identity that can be checked electronically. A law for a paper card only is not a yes.
revised criteria (map): The law in force provides for a digital identity and is in use: a source from the past three years counts people enrolled or identity numbers issued under it. A law for a paper card only does not reach this stage.
revised criteria (full): Question 3: Does the law provide for a digital identity, and are identities issued under it? A yes is: A source says the law in force sets up a biometric register, a unique identity number or an identity that can be checked electronically, and a source from the last three years counts people enrolled or numbers issued under it. A law for a paper card only is not a yes.

current criteria (map): Rules have been made under that law in the past three years: a regulation or decree applying it, or a rule that banks, phone companies or public bodies must check identity against the system. Cards issued, people enrolled and changes to fees do not count.
current criteria (full): Ladder 5 Mature: Yes to all four: rules have been made under that law in the last three years. Question 4: Have rules been made under it in the last three years? A yes is: A dated regulation or decree applying the law, or a dated rule made under it that banks, phone companies or public bodies must check identity against the system.
revised criteria (map): The law is applied beyond issuing identities: in the past three years an authority or court has decided under it, or banks, phone companies or public bodies check identity against the system because a rule under it requires them to. A rule made with no checks or decisions on record does not reach this stage.
revised criteria (full): Question 4: Is the law applied beyond issuing identities? A yes is: In the last three years: a dated decision, penalty or ruling by the identity authority or a court under the law, or a source showing banks, phone companies or public bodies checking identity against the system under a rule made under it. A regulation or decree made, with no checks or decisions on record, is not a yes.

current criteria (map): The law in force requires public bodies to share: to exchange data, to connect to the government's exchange platform, or not to ask a person for what another public body already holds. A law that only allows sharing does not reach this stage.
current criteria (full): Ladder 4 Operating: Yes to 1, 2 and 3: it requires public bodies to share. Question 3: Does it require public bodies to share data, and not only allow it? A yes is: A source says the law in force obliges public bodies to exchange data, to connect to the government's exchange platform, or not to ask a person for what another public body already holds.
revised criteria (map): The law requires public bodies to share, and they do: a dated source from the past three years names a public body exchanging data, or connected to the government's exchange platform, because the law requires it. A law that only allows sharing does not reach this stage.
revised criteria (full): Question 3: Does it require public bodies to share, and do they? A yes is: A source says the law in force obliges public bodies to exchange data, connect to the government's exchange platform, or not ask a person for what another body holds, and a dated source from the last three years names a public body doing so because the law requires it.

current criteria (map): The law has been applied in the past three years: a regulation, decree or order has been made under it, or public bodies are named as exchanging data because it requires them to.
current criteria (full): Ladder 5 Mature: Yes to all four: it has been applied in the last three years. Question 4: Has it been applied in the last three years? A yes is: A dated regulation, decree or order made under it, or a dated source naming public bodies that exchange data because it requires them to.
revised criteria (map): The law is in regular use: a source from the past three years names three or more public bodies exchanging data because it requires them to, or counts them, or a decision or order enforces it. A regulation made under it alone does not reach this stage.
revised criteria (full): Question 4: Is the law in regular use? A yes is: In the last three years: a dated source naming three or more public bodies that exchange data because the law requires them to, or counting them, or a dated decision or order enforcing it. A regulation or decree made under it is not a yes.

current criteria (map): The national meteorological service holds ISO 9001 certification for its services.
current criteria (full): Ladder 5 Certified: Yes to 4. Question 4: Is the service ISO 9001-certified? A yes is: A source from the last three years says the national meteorological service holds ISO 9001 certification for its services.
revised criteria (map): The service's satellite-based warnings or forecasts reach their users: a source from the past three years counts people, farmers, districts or sectors receiving them, or reports action taken on a warning.
revised criteria (full): Question 4: Do its warnings reach users? A yes is: A source from the last three years counting people, farmers, districts or sectors receiving the national meteorological service's satellite-based warnings or forecasts, or reporting action taken on one (an evacuation, a planting decision, a response plan). ISO 9001 certification is not a yes.

current criteria (map): From 2024 on, the government signed a public-private partnership, concession or joint venture in which the private partner puts a named amount into a public digital project, or private investors paid into a state fund.
current criteria (full): Ladder 5 Mature: Yes to all four: and the government brought private money into a public project. Question 4: Has the government brought private money into a public digital project? A yes is: A signed public-private partnership, concession or joint venture in which the private partner puts a named amount into a public digital project, or a state fund that private investors have paid into, from 2024.
revised criteria (map): From 2024 on, private money has gone into a public digital project: under a public-private partnership, concession or joint venture the private partner has paid in or the works have started, or private investors have paid into a state fund. A signature alone does not count.
revised criteria (full): Question 4: Has private money gone into a public digital project? A yes is: From 2024: a dated source saying the private partner in a public-private partnership, concession or joint venture on a public digital project has paid in a named amount or begun the works, or that private investors have paid into a state fund. A signed agreement with nothing paid or started is not a yes.

current criteria (map): The country has designated its critical information infrastructure, or bound the operators of critical systems to report incidents to the national body.
current criteria (full): Ladder 4 Operating: Yes to 3: critical information infrastructure designated. Question 3: Has the country named its critical information infrastructure? A yes is: A source states the systems that count as critical were designated, or their operators required to report incidents to the national body.
revised criteria (map): Operators of critical systems work with the national body: a source from the past three years reports incidents they have reported to it, or an audit, inspection or drill of designated critical infrastructure. Designation alone does not reach this stage.
revised criteria (full): Question 3: Do the operators of critical systems work with the national body? A yes is: A source from October 2023 or later reporting incidents that operators of critical systems reported to the national body, or an audit, inspection or exercise of designated critical information infrastructure. A designation or a duty to report, with nothing done under it, is not a yes.

current criteria (map): The law is being implemented: in the past three years an appointed authority has registered organisations, taken breach reports, issued guidance or inspected.
current criteria (full): Ladder 4 Operating: The law is being implemented: the authority registers organisations, takes breach reports, issues guidance or inspects. Question 3: Is the law being implemented, in the last three years? A yes is: A dated source shows the authority registering organisations, taking breach reports, issuing guidance or inspecting.
revised criteria (map): The law is being implemented: in the past three years an appointed authority has registered organisations, taken breach reports or inspected. Guidance issued alone does not reach this stage.
revised criteria (full): Question 3: Is the law being implemented, in the last three years? A yes is: A dated source shows the authority registering organisations, taking breach reports or inspecting. Guidance or a notice issued is not a yes.

current criteria (map): Public bodies are required to use the standards: a law, decree, regulation or circular makes them compulsory for the systems public bodies build or buy. A text that says of itself that it is compulsory does not count.
current criteria (full): Ladder 4 Operating: Yes to 1, 2 and 3: public bodies are required to use them. Question 3: Are public bodies required to use them? A yes is: A law, decree, regulation or circular that makes the standards compulsory for the systems public bodies build or buy.
revised criteria (map): A public system uses the standards: a dated source from the past three years names a government system built or bought to them, or exchanging data in the formats they set.
revised criteria (full): Question 3: Does a public system use them? A yes is: A dated source from the last three years naming a government system built, bought or exchanging data to the standards. A law, decree or circular making them compulsory, with no system named, is not a yes.

current criteria (map): A system has been checked against the standards in the past three years: a dated source names a public body, system or product tested, audited or certified against them, or gives a count. How good the standards are is not judged.
current criteria (full): Ladder 5 Mature: Yes to all four: a system has been checked against them in the last three years. Question 4: Has a system been checked against them in the last three years? A yes is: A dated source naming a public body, system or product tested, audited or certified against the standards, or giving a count of them.
revised criteria (map): The standards are compulsory and checked: a law, decree, regulation or circular makes them compulsory for public bodies' systems, and in the past three years a dated source names a system tested, audited or certified against them, or gives a count. How good the standards are is not judged.
revised criteria (full): Question 4: Are they compulsory and checked? A yes is: A law, decree, regulation or circular making the standards compulsory for the systems public bodies build or buy, and in the last three years a dated source naming a public body, system or product tested, audited or certified against them, or giving a count.

current criteria (map): An organisation can be certified against such a standard in the country: the standards body, or a certifier accredited in the country, offers certification against it or has certified an organisation. A certificate from a certifier abroad does not count.
current criteria (full): Ladder 4 Operating: Yes to 1, 2 and 3: certification against one is on offer in the country. Question 3: Can an organisation be certified against one in the country? A yes is: The standards body, or a certifier accredited in the country, offers certification against such a standard or has certified an organisation against it.
revised criteria (map): An organisation has been certified in the country against such a standard, by the standards body or a certifier accredited in the country. Certification on offer with none awarded does not reach this stage. A certificate from a certifier abroad does not count.
revised criteria (full): Question 3: Has an organisation been certified against one in the country? A yes is: A source naming an organisation certified against such a standard by the standards body or a certifier accredited in the country. Certification offered, with none awarded, is not a yes.

current criteria (map): A recovery plan or a failover test from the past three years is on record for that backup site.
current criteria (full): Ladder 4 Operating: Yes to 3: a recovery plan or test on record for it. Question 3: Is a recovery plan or test on record for it? A yes is: A source states that a disaster-recovery or continuity plan covers the government's backup, or that a failover test or recovery exercise was held.
revised criteria (map): The backup site has been used: a failover test or recovery exercise was held, or systems were restored or run from it, on record in the past three years. A recovery plan alone does not reach this stage.
revised criteria (full): Question 3: Has the backup been tested or used? A yes is: A source from the past three years stating that a failover test or recovery exercise was held on the government's backup site, or that systems were restored or run from it. A disaster-recovery or continuity plan alone is not a yes.

current criteria (map): The government's main data centre and its backup site are both Tier III or above.
current criteria (full): Ladder 5 Mature: Yes to 4: main and backup sites both Tier III or above. Question 4: Are the main and backup sites both Tier III or above? A yes is: Sources state that the government's main data centre and its backup site are each Tier III or IV, by certification, a TIA-942 rating or the operator's own statement.
revised criteria (map): The government's main data centre and its backup site are both Tier III or above, and failover to the backup has been tested more than once or used in an incident in the past three years.
revised criteria (full): Question 4: Are both sites Tier III, with failover tested repeatedly or used? A yes is: Sources stating that the main data centre and its backup site are each Tier III or IV, and that failover to the backup was tested two or more times, or used in an incident, in the past three years.

current criteria (map): A government open data portal is running under the policy. A statistics office's data portal, or one a donor or development bank runs for the country, does not count.
current criteria (full): Ladder 4 Operating: Yes to 1, 2 and 3: a government portal is running under it. Question 3: Is a government open data portal running under it? A yes is: A national portal the government runs, opened or reported at work, that a source ties to the policy or that the body responsible for the policy runs.
revised criteria (map): A government open data portal is running under the policy, and a public body has released data on it in the past three years. A portal launched with nothing released does not reach this stage.
revised criteria (full): Question 3: Is data being released on a portal under it? A yes is: In the last three years: a dated source naming a ministry or agency that has released data on a government portal tied to the policy. A portal opened, with no release on record, is not a yes.

current criteria (map): Public bodies have published data under the policy in the past three years: a source names a ministry or agency that has released data, or counts the datasets or the bodies publishing. How good the policy is, and how open the licence, is not judged.
current criteria (full): Ladder 5 Mature: Yes to all four: public bodies have published data under it in the last three years. Question 4: Have public bodies published data under it? A yes is: In the last three years: a dated source naming a ministry or agency that has released data on the portal or under the policy, or counting the datasets or the bodies publishing.
revised criteria (map): Public bodies publish regularly under the policy: a source from the past three years names three or more ministries or agencies publishing, or counts the datasets or bodies, or reports the data downloaded or reused. How good the policy is, and how open the licence, is not judged.
revised criteria (full): Question 4: Do public bodies publish under it across government? A yes is: In the last three years: a dated source naming three or more ministries or agencies releasing data under the policy, or counting the datasets or bodies, or giving downloads or reuses of the data.

current criteria (map): In the past three years parliament repealed, or a court of the country struck down, an offence of criminal defamation, false news, sedition or insulting the head of state.
current criteria (full): Ladder 4 Operating: Yes to 1, 2 and 3: and a law that punished speech has gone. Question 3: Has a law that punishes speech been repealed or struck down in the last three years? A yes is: Parliament repealing, or a court of the country striking down, an offence of criminal defamation, false news, sedition or insulting the head of state.
revised criteria (map): In the past three years a court of the country struck down or refused to apply an offence of criminal defamation, false news, sedition or insulting the head of state, or acquitted a journalist or critic charged under one. A repeal by parliament alone does not reach this stage.
revised criteria (full): Question 3: Has a court protected speech in the last three years? A yes is: A dated ruling of a court of the country striking down, or refusing to apply, an offence of criminal defamation, false news, sedition or insulting the head of state, or acquitting a journalist or critic charged under one.

current criteria (map): In the past three years a law, a ruling of the country's own court that a cut was unlawful, or an undertaking given in court barred the government from cutting the internet.
current criteria (full): Ladder 5 Mature: Yes to all four: and the government is barred from cutting the internet. Question 4: Has the government been barred from cutting the internet in the last three years? A yes is: A law, a ruling of the country's own court that a cut was unlawful, or an undertaking the government or regulator gave in court not to cut.
revised criteria (map): The bar on cutting the internet has held: a law, a ruling of the country's own court or an undertaking given in court bars the government from cutting it, and the internet stayed on through a national election or large protest since, on a source from the past three years.
revised criteria (full): Question 4: Has the bar on cutting the internet held? A yes is: A law, a ruling of the country's own court that a cut was unlawful, or an undertaking the government or regulator gave in court not to cut, and a dated source from the last three years saying the internet stayed on through a national election or large protest held since.

current criteria (map): A national law, decree or regulation has been passed or amended to give effect to a shared text. A draft, a consultation or a study does not count.
current criteria (full): Ladder 4 Operating: Yes to 1, 2 and 3: a national law or rule gives effect to it. Question 3: Has a national law or rule been passed that gives effect to one? A yes is: A dated source saying a national law, decree or regulation was passed or amended to carry out, transpose or bring national law into line with a named shared text. A draft, a consultation or a study is not a yes.
revised criteria (map): A national law giving effect to a shared text is in force and in use: in the past three years a licence, certificate, signature, decision or request has been made under it. A law passed with nothing done under it does not reach this stage.
revised criteria (full): Question 3: Is a national law giving effect to one in use? A yes is: A national law, decree or regulation passed or amended to give effect to a named shared text, and a dated source from the last three years naming a licence, certificate, signature, decision or request made under it.

current criteria (map): Something the country agreed has been put into effect: roaming charges cut with a neighbour, a joint body set up and meeting, a regional guideline adopted as a national rule, or a shared service opened.
current criteria (full): Ladder 4 Operating: Yes to 1, 2 and 3: something agreed put into effect. Question 3: Has anything it agreed been put into effect? A yes is: A dated source saying a thing agreed has started in the country: roaming charges cut or removed with a neighbour, a joint committee or council set up, a regional guideline or strategy adopted as a national rule or plan, a shared service opened.
revised criteria (map): Something the country agreed is working: roaming charges cut with a neighbour and in force, a joint body set up and meeting, or a shared service opened. A regional guideline adopted as a national rule, with nothing put to work, does not reach this stage.
revised criteria (full): Question 3: Is anything it agreed working? A yes is: A dated source saying a thing agreed is working in the country: roaming charges cut or removed with a neighbour and charged at the new rate, a joint committee or council meeting, or a shared service open. A regional guideline or strategy adopted as a national rule or plan is not a yes.

indicator: Robustness of government hardware and software (infra.capacity--robustness-of-government-hardware-and-software)
current criteria (map): The government has published an enterprise architecture or an inventory of its systems.
current criteria (full): Ladder 5 Mature: Yes to 4: a published architecture or inventory. Question 4: Has the government published a map of its systems? A yes is: A source states an enterprise architecture or an inventory of government systems was published or adopted.
revised criteria (map): The core systems' performance in service is reported: a source from the past three years gives uptime, transactions processed or users for one or more of them, or an audit of them in operation, such as by the auditor general.
revised criteria (full): Question 4: Is the core systems' performance in service reported? A yes is: A source from October 2023 or later giving uptime, transactions processed or users for the financial management, tax or payroll system, or an audit of one in operation (by the auditor general or another body). A published enterprise architecture or inventory is not a yes.

current criteria (map): Services on two different satellite networks are on sale, such as Starlink and a OneWeb or Konnect service.
current criteria (full): Ladder 4 Operating: Yes to 3: on sale from two satellite networks. Question 3: Is it on sale from more than one satellite network? A yes is: A source states that services on two different satellite networks are on sale, for instance Starlink and a OneWeb or Konnect service; two resellers of one network count once.
revised criteria (map): Satellite broadband is in use on two different satellite networks: a source from the past three years reports households, businesses or public sites connected on each.
revised criteria (full): Question 3: Is it in use on two satellite networks? A yes is: A source from the past three years reporting households, businesses or public sites connected on each of two different satellite networks; two resellers of one network count once. On sale alone is not a yes.

current criteria (map): A decree, regulation or order has been made under the law: on the statistics office, the statistics council or board, the approval of surveys or the confidentiality of data.
current criteria (full): Ladder 4 Operating: Yes to 1, 2 and 3: rules made under it. Question 3: Have rules been made under it to put it to work? A yes is: A dated decree, regulation or order made under the law: setting up or organising the statistics office, the statistics council or the board, or on how surveys are approved and data kept confidential.
revised criteria (map): The law is in use: in the past three years the council or board it sets up was appointed or met, or a survey approval, standard or release calendar was issued under it. A decree made under the law alone does not reach this stage.
revised criteria (full): Question 3: Has the law been used? A yes is: A dated act from the last three years done under the law: the council or board it sets up appointed or meeting, the head of the office appointed under it, or a standard, release calendar or survey approval issued under it. A decree or regulation made under it is not a yes.

current criteria (map): The law has been applied in the past three years: its council or board appointed or meeting, a standard, release calendar or survey approval issued under it, a rule made under it, or a penalty. A census or survey carried out, a strategy or a budget does not reach this stage.
current criteria (full): Ladder 5 Mature: Yes to all four: the law applied in the last three years. Question 4: Has it been applied in the last three years? A yes is: A dated act a source says was done under the law: the council or board it sets up appointed or meeting, the head of the office appointed under it, a standard, release calendar or survey approval issued under it, a rule made under it, or a penalty.
revised criteria (map): The law is in regular use: sources from the past three years show the office or council acting under it year after year, such as releases published to its calendar, surveys approved or other bodies' statistics certified as official, or a penalty imposed under it. A census or survey carried out, a strategy or a budget does not reach this stage.
revised criteria (full): Question 4: Is the law in regular use? A yes is: Sources from the last three years showing acts under the law in two or more years (releases on the calendar it sets, survey approvals, other bodies' statistics certified as official), or a dated penalty imposed under it. A rule made under it is not a yes.

indicator: Sustainable domestic financing of digital transformation (finance.budget--sustainable-domestic-financing-of-digital-transformation)
current criteria (map): In the past three years a fund, levy or tax assigned by law to digital programmes was created, collected money or paid for a project, or the government put state money to a digital programme it had said the country must pay for itself. A fund abolished, or held only in an old law, does not count.
current criteria (full): Ladder 4 Operating: Yes to 1, 2 and 3: and the government said it must be paid for at home, and acted. Question 3: Has the government said digital transformation must be paid for from the country's own resources, and acted on it, in the last three years? A yes is: A dated statement by the head of state, a minister, a budget speech or a national strategy, **and** an act that follows it: a fund, levy or tax assigned to digital programmes by law, or state money put to the programme the statement named. A law creating such a fund or levy is both at once.
revised criteria (map): In the past three years a fund, levy or tax assigned by law to digital programmes collected money or paid for a project, or the government put state money to a digital programme it had said the country must pay for itself. A fund created with nothing collected or paid, abolished, or held only in an old law does not count.
revised criteria (full): Question 3: Has the government said digital transformation must be paid for from the country's own resources, and has money moved, in the last three years? A yes is: A dated statement by the head of state, a minister, a budget speech or a national strategy, and money that follows it: a fund, levy or tax assigned to digital programmes by law that collected money or paid for a project, or state money put to the programme the statement named. A law creating a fund or levy, with nothing collected or paid, is not a yes.

current criteria (map): Taxes can be paid online, by bank transfer or by mobile money, through the tax authority's system.
current criteria (full): Ladder 4 Electronic payment: Yes to 3. Question 3: Can taxes be paid electronically? A yes is: A source from the last three years says taxes can be paid online, by bank transfer or by mobile money, through the tax authority's system.
revised criteria (map): Taxes are paid electronically through the tax authority's system: a source from the past three years reports payments made online, by bank transfer or by mobile money. A service that allows it, with no payments reported, does not reach this stage.
revised criteria (full): Question 3: Are taxes paid electronically? A yes is: A source from the last three years reporting taxes paid online, by bank transfer or by mobile money through the tax authority's system, or giving a figure for such payments.

current criteria (map): Online filing is mandatory for some taxpayers, or half or more of returns are filed online.
current criteria (full): Ladder 5 Mostly online: Yes to 4. Question 4: Is online filing mandatory or used by most? A yes is: A source from the last three years says online filing is mandatory for some taxpayers, or puts the share of returns filed online at half or more.
revised criteria (map): Half or more of returns are filed online, on a figure from the past three years. Online filing made mandatory, with no share published, does not reach this stage.
revised criteria (full): Question 4: Is online filing used by most? A yes is: A source from the last three years putting the share of returns filed online at half or more. A rule making online filing mandatory is not a yes.

indicator: Think tanks and academic departments contributing to DT policy (capacity.research--think-tanks-and-academic-departments-contributing-to-dt-policy)
current criteria (map): A local research institution holds a standing advisory role in digital policy, or a national research agenda on digital transformation is adopted.
current criteria (full): Ladder 5 Standing role: Yes to 4. Question 4: Is the role standing? A yes is: A source from the last three years says a local research institution holds a standing advisory role in digital policy, or a national research agenda on digital transformation is adopted.
revised criteria (map): Local research has shaped digital policy: in the past three years a law, strategy or policy cites a local institution's research, or a local institution in a standing advisory role has given its view on a named digital policy. A research agenda adopted, or a role held with no view given, does not count.
revised criteria (full): Question 4: Has local research shaped policy? A yes is: A source from the last three years saying a digital law, strategy or policy cites a local institution's research, or that a local research institution holding a standing advisory role gave its view on a named digital policy. A national research agenda adopted is not a yes.

indicator: Use of AI in government administration (tech.ai--use-of-ai-in-government-administration)
current criteria (map): The government's authority for cross-government digital governance has issued rules for government bodies' use or purchase of AI, or published a register of the government's AI systems.
current criteria (full): Ladder 5 Rules or register: Yes to 4. Question 4: Are rules or a register for government AI published? A yes is: A source from the last three years says the government's authority for cross-government digital governance has issued rules for government bodies' use or purchase of AI, or published a register of the government's AI systems.
revised criteria (map): Government use of AI is measured: a source from the past three years gives figures for a government AI system in service, such as queries answered, documents processed or cases handled, or the government publishes a register of the AI systems in use. Rules on using or buying AI alone do not reach this stage.
revised criteria (full): Question 4: Is government use of AI measured? A yes is: A source from the last three years giving figures of use or results for a government AI system in service (queries answered, documents processed, cases handled, time saved), or a register published by the government's authority for digital governance listing the AI systems in service. Rules for government bodies' use or purchase of AI, on their own, are not a yes.

current criteria (map): Two or more public bodies publish data that way, named or counted by a source from the past three years.
current criteria (full): Ladder 4 Several bodies: Yes to 3: two or more public bodies publish. Question 3: Do several public bodies publish data that way? A yes is: A source from the last three years names two or more public bodies publishing data on a portal, or counts the bodies publishing.
revised criteria (map): Data published that way is reused: a source from the past three years names an application, service, study or news story built on a public body's open data, or the portal reports downloads.
revised criteria (full): Question 3: Is the open data reused? A yes is: A source from the last three years naming an application, service, study or news story built on data a public body publishes under an open licence, or giving downloads from the portal. Data published, with no reuse on record, is not a yes.

current criteria (map): Four or more public bodies publish data that way, named or counted by a source from the past two years.
current criteria (full): Ladder 5 Four or more bodies: Yes to 4: four or more public bodies publish, on a source from the last two years. Question 4: Do four or more public bodies publish data that way? A yes is: A source from the last two years names four or more public bodies publishing data on a portal, or counts them at four or more.
revised criteria (map): Four or more public bodies publish data that way, and its reuse is counted: downloads, API calls or users given by a source from the past two years.
